_note: WHICH WAVE TABLE BELONGS TO WHICH LEVEL, and nothing more yet. It exists because level 2 stopped sharing level 1's waves and something has to say so; it is data, and no scene reads it. GameScene still loads waves.json directly and is still single-level on purpose — making it level-aware is a separate refactor and is not approved.
_lane: laneLengthPx is the walked length of the painted road, summed over the level's waypoints, rounded to 0.1. BOTH are now measured from the level's own map file by that one method: level 1 from map.json, level 2 from map_level2.json. Level 2 previously carried 1916.7, a figure that arrived with the plate before the lane was traced and was never checked; the traced waypoints walk 1955.3, so it was short by 38.6 px. It is recorded because wave spacing is only comparable between levels that walk the same distance, and the two here differ by 1.1%, which is not enough to retune. Re-measure after any retrace rather than carrying a number forward.
_unlock: runsClearedToUnlock is how many runs must be cleared before a level can be picked, counted by Save.runsCleared. It IS enforced: the title screen greys a locked level and START RUN re-checks the count before handing the level to the run. Level 2 was held at 99 while it was unwinnable; its pads have since been moved inside tower range and its wave health cut, so it is back to 1.
_mapPosition: WHERE A LEVEL SITS ON THE WORLD MAP, normalised 0-1 against the world's own bounds, and the ONLY place that position lives. WorldMapScene multiplies it by the world size; the trail between the cards is generated from these numbers rather than drawn, so moving a card moves the trail with it. Adding a level means a row here with a mapPosition and a card in art.json's worldMap.cards — a test fails the build if either is missing.
